newsitem.title: UK: London Clubs says first half trading strong.
newsitem.headline: London Clubs says first half trading strong.

text.p: Casino operator London Clubs International Plc on Thursday reported virtually static first-half pre-tax profits but said trading had been strong.
Pre-tax profits were 19.9 million stg compared with 19.8 million stg in the same period a year ago.
"Trading in the first half has again been strong," it said in a statement.
Turnover increased by nine percent to 94.3 million stg from 86.5 million, while earnings per share rose to 8.9p from 8.8p.
The first-half dividend was increased to 2.625 pence per share versus 2.5 pence last time.
But the company said its Ritz casino in central London "suffered from an unusually low win/drop percentage" which depressed profits at the Ritz substantially.
It said it would move the Ritz casino to new premises on St James's Street in central London once the current lease has expired.

"We believe that the current premises do not afford us the flexibility of the new site, which is considerably larger and will cater superbly for the changing demands of our upmarket clientele," it said.
